title: Organic symmetry reflects equilibrium and is absent without it, as in amoeba

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Organic symmetry reflects equilibrium and is absent without it, as in amoeba

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Symmetry is highly characteristic of organic forms because they are figures of equilibrium governed by a principle of minimal energy, as in liquid films; symmetry is lacking only where equilibrium is lacking, as in the amoeba.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Such symmetry is in a high degree characteristic of organic forms, and is rarely absent in living things,—save in such cases as amoeba, where the equilibrium on which symmetry depends is likewise lacking.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Minimal energy, equilibrium and symmetry”. Scope: organic forms generally, especially cells

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.57

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Symmetry and dynamics can be measured, and obvious counterexamples could refute a strict reading. Demonstrating the proposed minimal-energy cause rather than developmental regulation requires matched force and energy measurements rarely available broadly.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify symmetry and dynamic equilibrium or shape fluctuations across resting and motile organisms, and test whether departures from equilibrium predict asymmetry after controlling lineage and function. A stable asymmetric organism or symmetric nonequilibrium state would refute the categorical relation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim's exceptions and scope are vague.

Equilibrium and minimal energy are not directly observed from shape alone.

Biological symmetry is inherited and actively maintained.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.45
data adequacy: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.55
data existence: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.6

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Symmetry of organisms and the irregular outline of amoebae are observable, but the claim uses symmetry as the mark of equilibrium and equilibrium as the cause of symmetry. No dataset outcome would favour that principle over other pattern-forming mechanisms that also yield symmetric bodies. The statement is therefore not empirically decidable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim equates organic symmetry with equilibrium under minimal energy and cites the amoeba as the case where both are missing. Symmetry is the evidence offered for equilibrium, so the association cannot be tested against a rival force law.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Equilibrium is inferred from the symmetry it is then used to explain.

Asymmetric amoebae are compatible with many force laws, including ones far from a liquid film.
